title: Edmund and the Songbook
premise: Eleven years ago, marine biologist Ivo Coldharbour fled the island town of Saltmere after a betrayal by his first love, Edmund, leaving behind an unsent letter that never reached its recipient. When a storm-damaged post office finally delivers that letter to Edmund's widowed mother, Ivo is forced back for one last field season counting sea turtles before his research grant—and the island's ferry service—shut down for winter. As he and Edmund, now the town's embattled harbormaster fighting a corrupt developer seizing the waterfront, rebuild what was broken, they uncover proof that the developer's land claims were forged with help from the very officials Edmund trusted. At the climax, Ivo must choose between a prestigious mainland post and testifying at the hearing that could save Saltmere; he stays, the fraud collapses, and Edmund chooses him openly as the last ferry of the season leaves without either of them aboard.
about_author: Ulyana Thornbury is the pen name of a former lighthouse keeper's daughter who spent a decade cataloguing tide pools before turning to fiction. She writes romances about people who mistake solitude for safety, from a cottage overlooking the North Atlantic.

chapters.title: The Letter That Took Eleven Years
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. In his mainland lab, Ivo receives a water-stained envelope—his own handwriting, postmarked eleven years prior, returned undelivered after the Saltmere post office flood. Inside is the letter he wrote Edmund the night he left. He tells himself he'll burn it; instead he books a ferry ticket. Beat: dread disguised as scientific curiosity.

chapters.title: Turtle Season
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo arrives in Saltmere for his final nesting survey, hiding behind transect lines and data sheets. The town has changed; the harbor is half-scaffolded under a development called Meridian Point. He learns Edmund Voss is now harbormaster. Beat: the past made physical, avoidance through routine.

chapters.title: Harbormaster
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund spots Ivo on the dock and nearly drops his clipboard. Eleven years of anger curdle into something more complicated when he sees how thin Ivo has become. He says only 'You're late,' and walks away. Beat: wounded pride masking relief that Ivo came back at all.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brought Back
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Surveying a cove, Ivo finds an old tin box in the wrack line containing childhood keepsakes—their shared collection from the summer they fell in love. Edmund appears; they argue about who abandoned whom. Neither mentions the letter. Beat: grief surfacing as blame.

chapters.title: Meridian Rising
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Developer Cassian Roe hosts a gala on the half-built pier, courting the town council. Edmund notices councilman Aldous Pike signing documents too quickly and a survey map whose boundaries don't match the county records. He pockets a photocopy. Beat: first thread of suspicion, duty over heartbreak.

chapters.title: Nest 12
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Working nights monitoring a loggerhead nest, Ivo runs into Edmund doing midnight harbor checks. They fall into old rhythms—coffee from a thermos, silence that doesn't hurt yet. Edmund asks why Ivo really left. Ivo lies: 'a job.' Beat: fragile truce built on shared darkness.

chapters.title: Mother Knows the Postmark
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund's mother, Maren, shows him the delivered letter, unopened, saying it isn't hers to read. Edmund takes it but can't break the seal. Instead he confronts Ivo on the beach; Ivo admits he wrote it the night he left and thought it lost. Edmund walks into the surf rather than hear more. Beat: the wound reopened deliberately.

chapters.title: The Forged Line
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Comparing the photocopied map against county archives, Edmund confirms Meridian's easement crosses protected wetlands on paper signed by someone impersonating the previous harbormaster—Edmund's dead father. Pike's signature matches. Beat: personal grief weaponized into purpose.

chapters.title: An Ally With a Boat
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo offers his research boat and permit access to help document the wetlands before construction destroys them. Working together, their hands brush over charts; neither pulls away. Edmund admits he never stopped reading the tide tables Ivo taught him. Beat: partnership becoming intimacy.

chapters.title: Roe Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Cassian Roe offers Ivo a funded coastal institute position—if his environmental surveys come back 'ambiguous' and he distances himself from the harbormaster. Ivo, drowning in debt and career failure, doesn't say no. Beat: temptation wearing a professional face.

chapters.title: The Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. A hurricane shifts toward Saltmere. Edmund evacuates the marina while Ivo races to secure the turtle nests. They shelter together in the lighthouse as the island loses power, and in the dark Edmund finally opens the eleven-year-old letter. Beat: confession by candlelight—Ivo left because Edmund's father threatened to out him and ruin them both.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The storm wrecks Meridian's unfinished pier and exposes buried construction debris illegally dumped in the sanctuary—a crime with Roe's company name on it. Edmund and Ivo photograph everything before the tide erases it. In the wreckage, Edmund takes Ivo's hand. Beat: disaster as revelation, tenderness amid ruin.

chapters.title: Pike's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund confronts Aldous Pike privately; Pike confesses he forged the signatures under pressure from Roe and agrees to testify—but warns that Roe owns judges on the mainland. Pike slips Edmund the original forged deed. Beat: justice beginning outside official channels.

chapters.title: Two Weeks Left
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The seasonal ferry schedule ends in two weeks; after that, Ivo is stranded until spring or gone for good. Roe's institute offer still stands. He and Edmund stop pretending—they spend a night together that feels like coming home. Beat: happiness shadowed by a countdown.

chapters.title: Maren's Blessing
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Maren reveals she knew about the boys all along and kept Edmund's father's threats secret out of shame. She gives Edmund a second letter—her own apology—and tells him not to let Ivo leave twice. Beat: found family mending what blood family broke.

chapters.title: The Ambiguous Report
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Roe publishes Ivo's doctored survey data to greenlight construction. Ivo's name is on it. Devastated, he drafts a public retraction detailing the forgery, knowing it will end his career. Edmund finds him at dawn and says, 'Tell the truth. We'll survive it.' Beat: the choice crystallized.

chapters.title: Retraction
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo submits his sworn statement and the nest-site evidence to the county hearing, torching his reputation in academic circles. Roe retaliates—threatening litigation and revealing Ivo's past institutional blacklisting. Ivo realizes Roe engineered his original disgrace years ago to keep Saltmere's coast clear. Beat: sacrifice met with escalation.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. At the county courthouse, Pike testifies, the forged deed is entered, and Ivo dismantles Roe's survey on the stand with eleven years of turtle data proving the wetlands are critical habitat. Roe's lawyer produces the mainland job offer as proof of Ivo's bias—it backfires, showing coercion. Beat: climax; truth as the only weapon left.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The county voids Meridian's permits and refers Roe for prosecution; Pike resigns. The town celebrates on the broken pier, and Edmund kisses Ivo in front of everyone—no more past tense. But Ivo's mainland offer expires at week's end, and the last ferry looms. Beat: victory shadowed by departure.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Ferry day. Edmund waits at the dock expecting goodbye. Ivo arrives—not with luggage, but with his research equipment transferred to the Saltmere station and a resignation letter to the mainland institute. 'Someone has to count the turtles,' he says. 'It might as well be both of us.' Beat: choosing to stay made concrete.

chapters.title: Winter Harbor
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. First snow on the water. Ivo and Edmund repair the lighthouse cottage together, Maren downstairs baking, Pike stopping by with contrition and cider. Ivo mails a new letter—this one addressed, stamped, and full of everything he used to hide. Beat: quiet joy, home rebuilt from salvage.

chapters.title: Edmund and the Songbook
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Spring returns; the turtles nest again. Edmund finds the old songbook from their boyhood—sea shanties Ivo once transcribed—and Ivo adds a final page: a new song with both their names in it. The ferry returns with the season, carrying visitors to a town that stayed itself. Beat: the past tense becomes present, then future.
